Thought: To solve this problem, we need to consider the thermodynamic properties of A-T and G-C base pairs and how these properties affect the incorporation of strands into the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC). A-T base pairs are generally less stable (more thermodynamically unstable) than G-C base pairs because they form two hydrogen bonds compared to the three hydrogen bonds in G-C base pairs. This instability is advantageous at the 5' end of the antisense strand to promote its loading into the RISC. Therefore, incorporating A-T residues at the 5' region of the antisense sequence and G-C residues at the 5' region of the sense sequence is likely to facilitate the correct strand being loaded into the RISC.
